cues.text: September 2026. A Grade 5 pupil in Legazpi wakes up with a high fever.
cues.onscreen: "SEPTEMBER 2026"; a house at dawn; a pupil with a thermometer; the badge "DENGUE" fades in.

cues.text: The clinic writes down one thing first: her home address.
cues.onscreen: A case-report card slides in: "Case report · Address: home barangay"; a pin drops on the house.

cues.text: But the mosquito that bit her was not at home. It was at school, in the middle of the day.
cues.onscreen: The sun rises; a dotted path runs from the house to the school; an Aedes mosquito circles the school; the house pin greys out.

cues.text: Zoom out to Albay.
cues.onscreen: Albay as a field of 720 barangay dots in 18 towns.

cues.text: By mid-September, the province had 2,179 cases and 14 deaths, 84 percent more than the year before.
cues.onscreen: Counters: 2,179 cases · 14 deaths · +84% vs the same period of 2025 (Jan 1 to Sept 12, 2026); source Daily Tribune, 2026.

cues.text: The province declared a state of calamity, and schools closed for a week of cleanup.
cues.onscreen: Badge "STATE OF CALAMITY"; a school with the sign "Closed Sept 14 to 18 · cleanup and fogging".

cues.text: Sustainable Development Goal 3 asks us to end epidemics like dengue.
cues.onscreen: Chips: "SDG 3.3 · end the epidemics of neglected tropical diseases" and "SDG 3.d · early warning".

cues.text: Every case is filed by home address, so the brigades go to the homes.
cues.onscreen: Test network D1 (synthetic): bars of cases by residence; B2 has the most; brigade markers move to B2.

cues.text: But Aedes aegypti bites by day, where people gather: classrooms, markets, terminals.
cues.onscreen: Daytime arrows flow from every barangay into B1, the poblacion with the central school and public market; B1 glows.

cues.text: Spray where cases live, and you may spray the wrong barangay.
cues.onscreen: Spray cloud over B2 while B1 stays red; stamp "WRONG PLACE?".

cues.text: So where is dengue really spreading, and how much control is enough?
cues.onscreen: Three lines build: "Where does it spread? · How much is enough? · When do we warn?"

cues.text: This is where MCS comes into play.
cues.onscreen: The letters M, C and S drop in, then unfold into Mathematical, Computational, Sciences.

cues.text: Mathematics writes each barangay's day as a matrix: who spends how many hours, and where.
cues.onscreen: Chain lights "Open data → Graph"; panel MATHEMATICS: the 6 × 6 residence-time matrix P of test network D1 fills in as a heat map; p_ii = 1 − ω_i, p_ij ∝ A_j e^(−βT_ij).

cues.text: Its largest eigenvalue gives the reproduction number, and dengue fades when it falls below one.
cues.onscreen: M = κ D_N P W Pᵀ, R0² = λ_max(S); dial shows R0 = 1.214 with the threshold line at 1.

cues.text: Computing splits that number into shares by place, and ranks the true hotspots.
cues.onscreen: Chain lights "Algorithm → Numbers"; panel COMPUTING: paired bars, cases by residence vs transmission by place; B1 rises to 42.6%.

cues.text: Optimisation finds the cheapest brigade plan that brings the number below one, with a certificate that nothing cheaper exists.
cues.onscreen: Chain lights "Optimisation"; panel OPTIMISATION: min Σ c_j u_j subject to R0(u) ≤ 0.95; cost bars for five strategies, least cost 22.60 team-days with its certified lower bound.

cues.text: On the test network, cases pointed to a residential barangay, but forty-three percent of transmission was at the school and market.
cues.onscreen: Two cards: "Most cases by home: B2, 28.5%" and "Most transmission by place: B1, 42.6%" (test network D1, synthetic).

cues.text: The least-cost plan needed forty percent fewer team-days than spraying everywhere.
cues.onscreen: Counter: 37.47 → 22.60 team-days, −40%; versus spraying where cases live 38.88 (−42%).

cues.text: And a CUSUM alarm warned more than a week and a half sooner than a single-week threshold.
cues.onscreen: CUSUM curve S_t climbs past h = 12.75; bars of mean delay: CUSUM 4.84 weeks vs single-week rule 6.52 weeks at the same 5% false-alarm rate (5,000 simulated years).

cues.text: Twelve results, proven, then verified against independent code.
cues.onscreen: Chain lights "Proof"; twelve proof squares turn into green checks; 300/300 reproduction numbers, 120/120 control plans, 10,000 alarm sequences.

cues.text: BANTA-Y will not kill one mosquito.
cues.onscreen: Boom. Screen darkens; the line appears in white.

cues.text: But it will tell the brigades where the bites really happen, and how much is enough.
cues.onscreen: The line appears in gold.

cues.text: [pause] Homes tell you where dengue is reported. Places tell you where it spreads.
cues.onscreen: Two lines: "Homes tell you where dengue is reported." (white), then "Places tell you where it spreads." (gold).
